extracted.intended_audience: prospective applicants (organizations and researchers) seeking Commonwealth Fund grants
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for organizations and researchers on preparing and submitting a Letter of Inquiry (LOI) and understanding the Commonwealth Fund's funding priorities, review process, and staff engagement in proposal development.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mission alignment
rubrics_metrics.description: The mission of the Commonwealth Fund is to promote a high-performing, equitable health care system that promotes better access, improved quality, and greater efficiency in health care for everyone — regardless of income, insurance status, geography, gender, race, ethnicity, or ability status — and especially for society’s most vulnerable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposals should advance the Fund’s mission by addressing access, quality, efficiency, and equity in health care and prioritizing benefits for vulnerable populations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Types of work the Fund supports
rubrics_metrics.description: The Fund carries out this mandate by supporting independent research on health care issues and making grants to improve health care practice and policy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fund-supported activities include demonstrating pioneering approaches and evaluating their results to identify levers for change; convening experts across backgrounds and disciplines to spark innovation and facilitate learning; disseminating the results of research to spur change; and investing in tomorrow’s health care leaders and their capacity to promote equitable outcomes both in the U.S. and abroad.

rubrics_metrics.name: How to apply: LOI submission method
rubrics_metrics.description: To apply for a grant from the Commonwealth Fund, please submit a letter of inquiry (LOI) using the online grants portal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants must use the Fund’s online grants portal to submit LOIs (links and portal instructions are provided on the site).

rubrics_metrics.name: Check current funding priorities before applying
rubrics_metrics.description: Before doing so, you may want to learn about the Fund’s current funding priorities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Review the Fund’s published funding priorities to assess fit prior to submitting an LOI; align project focus with those priorities to increase likelihood of being identified as a potential fit.

rubrics_metrics.name: LOI timing and deadlines
rubrics_metrics.description: LOIs are accepted on a rolling basis, unless they are submitted in response to a request for proposals (RFP), in which case the submission deadline is shown on the funding announcement and the portal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submit LOIs anytime for general funding opportunities; for RFP-driven opportunities, adhere to the posted deadline on the funding announcement and in the portal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notification timeline
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants are typically advised of the results of their inquiries within six weeks, and often sooner.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Expect a decision/response about an LOI within approximately six weeks; timelines may vary.

rubrics_metrics.name: If LOI is a fit — collaborative proposal development
rubrics_metrics.description: If your LOI is identified as a potential fit, program staff will be in touch about next steps in our collaborative proposal development process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When an LOI aligns with Fund priorities, staff engage with applicants and participate in collaborative development of a full proposal or next-stage materials.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligible grantee types (implied)
rubrics_metrics.description: In addition to giving grants to health care–focused organizations, Fund staff conduct their own research as well.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Primary grantees are health care–focused organizations (the site lists many institutional grantees as examples); individual staff-led research is also part of the Fund’s work. Use the grantee examples to gauge typical organizational types and scale.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fund staff role and communications expectation
rubrics_metrics.description: Fund staff are collaborative partners in the grantmaking process. In addition to giving grants to health care–focused organizations, Fund staff conduct their own research as well. Our communications team, meanwhile, helps to ensure the foundation is a leader in disseminating timely, actionable information to health care leaders, policymakers, community stakeholders, and the media.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants should anticipate staff engagement beyond awarding (e.g., collaboration, dissemination). Proposals that include dissemination plans and engagement with policymakers/stakeholders align with the Fund’s emphasis on spreading actionable findings.
